### [Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28947>)

This study compares structured 2:4 sparsity with lower-precision dense inference while counting index metadata, dynamic preprocessing and the hardware’s actual sparse operand constraints. Across the tested models and GPUs, it finds that quantizing further is usually the better next step when a lower supported precision remains, while sparsity at the tested precision floor can raise throughput but needs retraining to recover usable model quality.

**Published:** 2026-10-20 · **First seen:** 2026-10-22T10:07:28.843Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Structured Sparsity, Quantization, Hardware Evaluation, Quality Recovery

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28947>) · [Code](<https://github.com/PuppyQ08/24_quant_compare>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full21-page v1 paper inspected, including Sections3–6, all comparison/evaluation tables and AppendicesA–I, plus the author README and initial artifact tree/history. Metadata-inclusive bit accounting pairs 2:4 INT8 with dense INT5 (both5.125bits/original element with group128 FP16 scales), rather than incorrectly with INT4. Per-layer operator comparisons cover Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B across W/X/Q/K/V/attention probabilities; measured kernels use L40S, H100 and RTX PRO6000, including online pruning/quantization for dynamic operands. The strongest dense rival at a hardware tier dominates the tested sparse alternatives above the deployment precision floor; some sparse cases beat weaker quantizers or improve retrieval/perplexity, so this is not a universal all-metric ranking. On one H100, historical vLLM0.11.2 serves Llama-3.1-8B versus externally retrained13B-token Sparse-Llama; sparse FP8 prefill is74.6k versus58.9k tokens/s (64×2048-token prompts), with batch1 decode234 versus198 and batch64 decode9914 versus8556 tokens/s. The same sparse weights served densely remove the throughput benefit within3%, separating kernel gain from model differences. Original source date isOct20 receipt21:48:45Z; code repo created18:50:58Z and initial696a1107 commit19:59:45Z onOct20 already contains implementation and measurements. Although the original cs.LG paper batch isOct22, this unreported work is conservatively an editorial delayed discovery inside the72-hour lookback, not a new optimization first released in theOct22 main window. Commit timestamps do not prove exact historical public visibility; optional earliest-work public\_availability is therefore omitted.

**Limitations:** Two8B models, a finite quantizer/pruner menu and specific shapes/hardware support the conclusions; the precision floor is defined by the tested inference stack, explicitly excluding unused Ada INT4 tensor-core paths. Operator error is an imperfect whole-model proxy; GSM8K uses the first250 problems with8-shot greedy chain-of-thought and broad confidence intervals, and some retrieval/perplexity results favor sparsity. Sparse library algorithms receive exhaustive tuning while dense libraries use default heuristics. Accuracy-winning dynamic correction is omitted from sparse timing, and some low-bit comparisons are simulated rather than hardware kernels. The27% prefill result uses historical vLLM0.11.2, not current serving releases (Sparse24 was removed in0.19); no GSM8K difference in that serving table is significant. The author’s two1B-token retraining runs are single, untuned recipes on fourH100 each; the13B-token Sparse-Llama reference uses different training data, so recovery cost is not a controlled token-scaling law. Blackwell sparse FP4 requires pairwise4:8, distinct from element-wise2:4, and the limited retraining budget failed to recover reasoning. No independent reproduction was performed.

## [2026-10-21](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-21.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Humming: Unified Quantized Inference Kernels and New Serving Measurements](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-21-humming>)

Humming separates a model’s quantization description from hardware-specific execution choices, composing shared data movement, dequantization, scheduling and Tensor Core components into specialized kernels. The new engineering report shows how this design translates selected low-bit formats into practical dense and mixture-of-experts execution, with an explicit serving comparison that changes activation precision while preserving the checkpoint’s quantized weights.

Blog data is author/community reported, not independently reproduced. The October21 publication republishes prior source material; the October20 new end-to-end source update is explicitly preserved rather than resetting method/code age.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22870>)

This study traces instability in FP8 reinforcement learning to quantization errors that distort policy-update clipping and prevent undesirable outputs from receiving corrective gradients. Its Calibrated Clipping method periodically uses BF16 reference statistics to adjust clipping bounds, making low-precision rollout and training more stable across the tested reasoning models.

**Published:** 2026-09-19 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** FP8, Reinforcement Learning, Numerical Stability

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22870>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. GRPO and DAPO experiments cover 8B–32B Qwen models and multiple FP8 scaling granularities, with controlled analyses of entropy surges and recovery toward BF16 performance.

**Limitations:** Periodic calibration requires two BF16 shadow forward passes. Reported 1.1–1.5x throughput measurements isolate offline training and exclude calibration, so they do not establish end-to-end RL speedups; some accuracy gaps remain and code was not verified.
